title: Initialization Handoff & Background Hydration for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement an initialization handoff and background hydration subsystem that reduces cold starts for Dedicated fleets by pre-allocating runtime slots, asynchronously hydrating model weights and KV caches, and enabling tenant-affinity residency scoring. This ticket covers API, runtime orchestration, and rollout controls required to provide throughput guarantees and predictable autoscaling behavior for reserved capacity customers.

Motivation: Customers using Dedicated capacity experience sporadic cold starts when traffic bursts exceed active residency. Existing warm-pool logic loads weights aggressively at scale, but lacks controlled handoff between primed workers and incoming requests, and does not provide a visibly bounded cold-start tail for throughput SLAs. We need a more deterministic initialization strategy to meet throughput guarantees while minimizing wasted GPU residency and preserving cost-efficiency.

Goals: 
- Reduce p95+ tail latency from cold starts by >70% for tenant ramp-ups.
- Ensure fleet-level throughput guarantees remain achievable under bursty workloads with autoscaling enabled.
- Provide operator-level controls for slot preassignment, background hydration window, and eviction grace periods.
- Maintain security hygiene (KMS access for models, audit logs for prewarming operations).
design_notes:
High-level design: introduce a coordinator (warm-handshake-controller) that orchestrates three phases: slot reservation, background hydration, and live handoff. Slot reservation pins empty GPU slots (compute containers) for a tenant's upcoming traffic using a tenant-affinity score (historic qps, recent opens, SLA tier). Background hydration streams model checkpoints and KV cache snapshots into reserved slots using a throttled transfer pipeline that adapts based on network and disk IO metrics. Once hydration reaches a readiness threshold (weights+KV checksum ok, token-budget warm), the controller performs a handoff to mark the slot live and move it into request routing.

Important differences from prior work: avoid eager full-cluster preload of all weights (wasteful). Use staged hydration: critical tensors + KV prefixes first to provide partial warm responses fast, then background-optimize remaining weights. Add a fast-fallback path that serves from a lightweight micro-model (small quantized variant) while full weights finalize, so latency SLOs are preserved.

APIs & Config: 
- fleet.warmPool.slot_target: integer (min slots reserved per tenant)
- fleet.warmPool.hydration_window: seconds (max time to perform background hydration)
- fleet.warmPool.eviction_grace: seconds
- fleet.warmPool.partial_warm_threshold: percentage (e.g., 40%)
- flow: POST /v1/fleets/{id}/warm-handoff (admin) to trigger manual handoff

Security: hydration uses short-lived KMS credentials issued via the fleet control plane; audit events emitted to console and tenant audit-log.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Coordinator successfully reserves slots for at least three tenants concurrently in a staging fleet and hydrates them to partial_warm_threshold within hydration_window.
2) Handoff toggles slot into routing and requests are served from newly-hydrated slot; end-to-end latency measurements show p50/p95 improvements vs baseline.
3) Autoscaler respects slot reservations (does not evict reserved slots prematurely).
4) Admin APIs allow increasing/decreasing slot_target and performing manual handoffs.
5) Security review passed and prewarm audit events logged.
implementation_tasks: spec: warm-handshake-controller behavior and state machine
runtime: slot reservation API and persistence (etcd) updates
runtime: streaming hydration pipeline with backpressure and checksum validation
routing: handoff marker and fast-fallback route to micro-models
autoscaler: honor reservation contract and eviction grace-periods
console: controls for slot_target and dashboard for warm-pool health
integration tests and canary harness for a dedicated fleet in staging
security: KMS credential flow and audit logging
progress_updates: 2025-08-11: Kickoff meeting — aligned on coordinator design and staged hydration approach. Decided to adopt checksum-based readiness signals rather than arbitrary timers (Aisha).
2025-08-18: Prototype slot reservation schema committed (RFC posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/warm-handshake-proto).
2025-08-25: Implemented hydration worker skeleton and streaming checksum validator. Initial local tests show partial warm path reduces token-init latency by ~40%.
2025-08-29: Design review feedback from infra (Sanjay) — suggested adding eviction_grace and separating min_reserved per-SKU. Updated design to include per-model SKU reservation buckets.

2025-09-01: Began autoscaler integration branch. Early integration test uncovered race where autoscaler reclaimed slots while hydration still in-flight; added a reservation lease extension RPC to prevent premature eviction.
review_feedback: Infra (Sanjay Rana): Ensure reservation lease persists across controller restarts; use persisted locks in etcd and include TTL renewal. Also requested circuit-breaker when disk IO saturates.
Product (Lena Morris): Add admin knob to prefer cost-efficiency vs immediate throughput guarantees for customers on lower tiers.
Security (Rafiq Khan): KMS credential window needs to be bounded and rotated per-hydration; require audit events for each hydration start/complete/fail.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-reserving slots increases cost for Dedicated tenants. Mitigation: implement elasticity policy that decays slot_target on sustained low utilization and expose cost impact in console.
Risk: Hydration floods storage/network causing cluster instability. Mitigation: streaming pipeline with adaptive backpressure and global hydration QPS limiter; per-fleet congestion metrics exposed.

Risk: Incorrect readiness signaling leads to degraded accuracy if partial weights are used. Mitigation: only mark partial warm slots for low-cost/return-first responses and run regression evals on canary workloads before enabling for production tenants.
testing_plan: Unit tests for controller state transitions, integration tests with staging fleet (simulate burst ramp), load tests measuring p50/p95 cold-start latency, canary rollout that enables feature for 5% of Dedicated fleets, rollback path if throughput SLA breaches. Capture eval metrics and automatic alerting tied to quality regressions.
rollout_plan: Phase A (staging): deploy controller + hydration pipeline to staging fleets; run synthetic ramp tests. Phase B (canary): enable for 5% production fleets with monitoring and kill-switch. Phase C (wide): ramp to 50% then 100% with cost reporting enabled. Provide runbook for on-call to disable handoff or reduce slot_target.
followups: Instrument per-tenant cost telemetry for reserved slots (slices in cost dashboards)
Explore tenant-aware prefetch policies that leverage historical KV prefix access patterns
Investigate hybrid warm-cache where small hot-weights remain resident and larger slower weights are paged in lazily
notes: Decided to avoid monolithic full-weight preload — prefer staged hydration to balance cost and latency.
Consider adding a debug endpoint to surface hydration progress per-slot for faster on-call triage.
Ask SRE to validate network egress budget for large fleets when background hydration is enabled.
